subject: Banking
title: How Banks Approve Loans
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How Banks Approve Loans.

hook.text: A bank decides in seconds whether you get a loan. Algorithms score your credit, income, and debt before a human sees it.

buildup.text: Underwriting was once a human job. A banker met you, reviewed your finances, and made a judgment call.

discovery.text: Today, automated systems evaluate your application against hundreds of data points. Speed replaced personal judgment.

twist.text: A clean model can still reject good borrowers when proxies like zip code echo old bias.

climax.text: Automated lending is faster and cheaper but creates invisible bias. When a machine says no, there's nobody to appeal to.

punchline.text: Algorithms approve in seconds. Faster, but bias can hide in the data.

quiz.question: What concern exists with automated lending decisions?
options: Algorithms can encode bias through correlated data like zip codes
